clue.text: Old dear in the wrong file

indicators.note: letters that are in the wrong order are muddled, so the word file is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly lady has misplaced a document in the filing cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong' turns FILE into LIEF. 'Old' marks the definition as archaic: the word is now found mainly in old verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for beloved or cherished, as in Shakespeare's 'my lief lord'.

clue.text: Former Soviet organisation fighter knocked out first round

indicators.note: first tells us the round piece comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: a boxer knocked out is scrambled and senseless, so the fighter's letters are jumbled

parts.note: a pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer from the old USSR was flattened in the opening round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' looks like part of a boxing story but is the anagram signal, and 'first' fixes the round letter at the front. The OGPU was the Soviet secret police of the 1920s and 30s.
explanation.definitionFit: The secret police body of the early USSR, forerunner of the NKVD and KGB.

clue.text: Eat up, girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: to eat a meal is to dine

explanation.surface: Someone urges a young woman to finish her food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat up' looks like a single instruction to finish a plate; in a down entry 'up' reverses DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the writer Blyton.

clue.text: Lizard in form, perhaps

explanation.surface: A reptile seems to be in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' reads as 'on good form', but a form is a school class, and a pupil given duties in it is a monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical reptile of the varanid family; also a pupil given duties in a school class.

clue.text: Once lifted it makes a change of course

indicators.note: the words before it are worked into something new, so their letters are rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: Something raised once alters the direction of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it makes' signals that the ten letters of 'Once lifted' are reordered; 'Once lifted' looks like a description but is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning aside from a path, as a ball veering off a defender.

clue.text: Untouched land containing what the wise maidens shared?

explanation.surface: Unspoiled ground holds whatever the sensible young women had in common.
explanation.walkthrough: In the parable of the wise and foolish virgins the wise ones kept oil for their lamps, so their oil is the maidens' oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground never ploughed or cultivated; read as two words, the lamp oil belonging to the parable's maidens.

clue.text: Joint for one of Elia's sup porters

explanation.surface: A cut of meat suits one of an essayist's backers.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his essays as Elia, so his supporters, the things he stood on, are the legs of Lamb. The page splits 'supporters' across a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast cut of young sheep; also a limb of the essayist Charles Lamb, pen-name Elia.

clue.text: One to be cross as a goat

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be as bad-tempered as a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross as a goat' looks like a simile about temper; 'cross' gives X and 'goat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild mountain goat of the Alps with long curved horns.

clue.text: Died unwillingly?

parts.note: read not as dying reluctantly but as dying without having made a will

explanation.surface: Someone passed away against their wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying with no legal testament, so the estate passes under the law rather than by bequest.

clue.text: Stumbled upon by Heather, poor child

parts.note: to stumble upon something is to have found it
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A girl named Heather comes across an impoverished youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a girl's name but is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned infant discovered and taken in, hence a child to be pitied.

clue.text: What the Flanders Mare might well have done

definitions.text: What the Flanders Mare might well have done

parts.words: What the Flanders Mare might well have done
parts.note: Henry VIII called Anne of Cleves the Flanders Mare; a mare is a horse, and a wife might pester her husband

explanation.surface: A guess at the behaviour of Henry VIII's fourth wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both an old horse, fitting 'Mare', and a verb for scolding, fitting a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or pester persistently, as a resented queen might; also a word for a horse.

clue.text: Inclination to skirmish in the lists

explanation.surface: A tendency to pick fights at a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The lists were the fenced ground where knights jousted, and to joust there was to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or lean; also to charge with a lance in a joust.

clue.text: Individual on key

parts.note: E is ... of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A single person sits at a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A single person or thing, as in 'one at a time'.

clue.text: Food for a bighead

parts.note: loaf is slang for head, so a big head is a big loaf, which is also bread

explanation.surface: A meal fit for a conceited person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' means use your head (rhyming slang, loaf of bread = head), so a bighead is literally a big loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A big bread is something to eat, and in slang a big head.

clue.text: Wrinkle on the Customs Officer's brow?

definitions.text: Wrinkle on the Customs Officer's brow?

parts.words: Wrinkle on the Customs Officer's brow
parts.note: a wrinkle is a crease, and customs officers collect import tax

explanation.surface: A frown line on a border official's forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: A crease is a line and customs collect duty, so the officer's wrinkle is a line of duty, the phrase for one's job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for tasks done as part of one's job, read literally as a crease caused by tax work.

clue.text: Single orbit for an astronaut

parts.note: one circuit of the Earth goes out and comes back to the starting point

explanation.surface: A spaceman circles the planet just once.
explanation.walkthrough: A journey out and back is so called; an orbit is literally round, so one orbit is a trip that is round.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to a place and back again, here a single circling of the globe.

clue.text: Put on a show of calisthenics

definitions.text: Put on a show of calisthenics

parts.words: Put on a show of calisthenics
parts.note: put on a show suggests staging an event; a display of gymnastic drills is a workout

explanation.surface: Someone staged a gymnastics display.
explanation.walkthrough: The word also means used or exerted (a right, a skill) and worried, but here it is doing physical drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Did physical training such as keep-fit drills.

clue.text: Sherry perhaps, but additionally an old instrument

explanation.surface: A wine that is also an ancient musical device.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack was an old name for sherry-like white wine; add 'but' and you get the sackbut, an early trombone.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a dry white fortified wine; with 'but' added it names a Renaissance brass instrument.

clue.text: Made certain in the finish

annotationWithheld.why: Made certain in the finish (7): SURE (certain) inside END gives the letters, but 'certain' is then needed both in the definition 'Made certain' and as SURE

clue.text: Knight-errant for a youngster in discomfort

indicators.note: in tells us the youngster is placed inside the word for discomfort

parts.note: discomfort is pain
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A wandering knight steps in to help a child in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link; 'in' puts the youngster inside the discomfort. A paladin was originally one of Charlemagne's twelve peers.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Charlemagne's champions, hence any chivalrous wandering knight.

clue.text: Unpretentious Slater's manner

indicators.note: a manner is a way of doing things, so the letters are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Mr Slater has a modest way about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manner' tells you to rearrange SLATERS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and natural, without guile or affectation.

clue.text: There's plenty to choose from, by all the saints!

definitions.text: There's plenty to choose from, by all the saints!

parts.words: There's plenty to choose from, by all the saints
parts.note: reads as an exclamation, but saints are virtuous people, so a gathering of all of them is a range of the virtuous

explanation.surface: Someone surveys an ample range and swears by the saints.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a wide choice; a choice made only from saints would be a selection of the good.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide range of options; also a gathering of the virtuous.

clue.text: Main go-between for North and South America

definitions.text: Main go-between for North and South America

parts.words: Main go-between for North and South America
parts.note: main is an old word for the open sea, so this is a sea lying between the two continents

explanation.surface: A chief intermediary between the two halves of the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief' but means the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bounded by Central America, the Antilles and northern South America.

clue.text: A follower has it in part

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter after A is B

explanation.surface: A disciple holds something partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A follower' looks like a disciple but is the letter that follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece, as in 'a bit of cake'.

clue.text: Tailless Japanese fish

annotationWithheld.why: Tailless Japanese fish (3): TAIL with its last letter cut off gives TAI, but the one word 'Tailless' is both the fodder TAIL and the deletion indicator 'less', so a single clue word does two jobs

clue.text: Circular, letter on the German currency

indicators.note: on puts the round letter in front of the next piece

parts.note: a circular letter is the round letter O
der is the German for the

explanation.surface: A round letter is stamped on the German money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like money but means something with a current, a river: the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows with a current, making it a flowing thing, a crossword sense of 'currency'.

clue.text: See 20
Sailor finally rounding on copper in the 2l

indicators.note: on places the sailor piece after the copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: turning round at the end means the sailor is written backwards in last place

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman at last turns on a policeman in the islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is CU; 'finally rounding' turns AB into BA at the end. 21 across is the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: With a large following I'm leader

annotationWithheld.why: With a large following I'm leader (4): I'M + A + M fits, but no standard abbreviation gives M for 'large' (L is usual); the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: With a large following I'm leader

clue.text: Disagreeable voters

parts.note: disagreeable suggests unpleasant, but here it means those who vote against a motion

explanation.surface: Unpleasant people at the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament those against a motion are recorded under this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The votes, or voters, against a proposal in a division.

clue.text: Obstruct returning vessels

indicators.note: coming back means the word is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: pots are vessels

explanation.surface: Ships coming back into port block the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships; they are cooking pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or halt something.

clue.text: Part of the car that smashes a record, one hears

indicators.note: heard rather than read, so the words sound like the answer

parts.note: something that smashes a record makes a disc break

explanation.surface: A car component that shatters vinyl, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc breaks' sounds the same as the braking system.
explanation.definitionFit: Brakes in which pads grip a rotating metal plate on the wheel.
